items.name: Madred's Bloodrazor
items.description: 40 Attack Damage 40% Attack Speed 25 ArmorSeeing Red: Attacks deal 4% of the target's maximum Health as bonus magic damage on-hit.Deals a maximum of 120 bonus damage to monsters.
wikiNotes: It was best used on DPS (damage per second) champions when the other team had a lot of tanks with armor or health builds.
DPS champions could maximize the effect of this item by stacking it with attack speed items and other on hit items such as Malady, Ionic Spark and Wit's End.
The unique passive of Madred's Bloodrazor dealt magic damage. Therefore, the unique effect could have its damage reduced by magic resistance items such as Negatron Cloak.
Malady synergized with Madred's Bloodrazor since it reduced the magic resistance of your target with each hit.

Champions who can proc on hit effects multiple times in quick succession did best with this item, such as Warwick's Infinite Duress and Renekton's Ruthless Predator, which could result in the quick destruction of health stacking champions or tanks that lack magic resistance.
Madred's Bloodrazor Dominion counterpart is Kitae's Bloodrazor.

The item was removed because it gave too many odd stats, and its on-hit damage was magic damage which made it hard to put in an effective item build that would still synergize with the auto attacking champions that would build it (Warwick being one of the few exceptions). It was replaced with Blade of the Ruined King.
The Bloodrazor enchantment added the passive back to the jungle, as a callback to the original item.

wikiPassives.label: Unique - Cinderbloom:
wikiPassives.text: Your magic and true damage will critically strike for 120% damage against enemies below 40% maximum health.

wikiNotes: Cinderbloom uses the following formula to calculate the damage for its critical strike: increased damage=base damage+((base damage×0.2)×(product of all critical damage modifiers)).
For example, if an ability deals 100 damage by default, then it will critically strike for 120 damage: 120=100+(100×0.2).
If the user has a critical damage modifier such as Infinity Edge, the damage amplifier is increased to 26%. The ability will thus critically strike for 126 damage: 126=100+((100×0.2)×(1+0.3)).

If the target has critical strike damage reduction such as Randuin's Omen's Resilience, which counts as a critical damage modifier for Cinderbloom, the damage amplifier is reduced to 14%. The ability will thus critically strike for 114 damage: 114=100+((100×0.2)×(1+(−0.3))).

If the user has Infinity Edge and the target has Randuin's Omen, the damage amplifier is reduced to 18.2%, which is only slightly lower than the base amplifier of 20% due to the multiplicative nature of the modifiers. The ability will thus critically strike for 118.2 damage: 118.2=100+100×0.2×(1+0.3)×(1−0.3).

wikiPassives.label: Unique - Steadfast:
wikiPassives.text: Taking magic damage from champions generates a stack of Steadfast for 7 seconds, stacking up to 8 times with the duration refreshing on subsequent magic damage from them and whenever dealing damage to them. Becoming immobilized by an enemy champion generates 2 stacks and also refreshes the duration. Once per cast instance, each incoming basic attack, ability, or item effect can only generate 1 stack of Steadfast from their damage every 1 second. At maximum stacks, gain 70 bonus magic resistance and 6% bonus movement speed.

wikiNotes: All champion abilities generate stacks of Steadfast when dealing magic damage to the user.
Lethal Tempo, Scorch, and Shield Bash generate stacks of Steadfast when dealing magic damage to the user, other runes do not.
Infernal Dragon Soul generates stacks of Steadfast when dealing magic damage to the user.
Fated Ashes' Inflame grants stacks of Steadfast more than once per second, even if its magic damage concides with another damage instance, independently of cast instance.(bug)
Some item effects do not generate stacks of Steadfast when dealing magic damage to the user.(bug)

These include: Ardent Censer's Sanctify, Bami's Cinder, Hollow Radiance, and Sunfire Aegis' Immolate, Guinsoo's Rageblade's Wrath, Hollow Radiance's Desolate, Imperial Mandate's Coordinated Fire, Malignance's Hatefog, Statikk Shiv's Electrospark, Stormsurge's Squall, Unending Despair's Anguish, and Zeke's Convergence's Frostfire Tempest.
All other item effects will properly generate stacks. Click the Show tab below for a list of them.

items.name: Crystalline Flask
items.description: Replenishment: Holds 3 charges and refills upon visiting the shop. ActiveConsumes a charge to restore 120 Health and 60 Mana over 12 seconds.
wikiNotes: The active cannot be used simultaneously with Health Potion and Mana Potion.
The sell value of this item is 40% of the total cost.
Compared to potions each charge is worth 49 gold (28 for health and 21 for mana) or 53.9 gold (30.8 for health and 23.1 for mana) when using the Alchemist mastery.

Assuming you eventually sell it, Crystalline Flask breaks even with regular potions once a champion consumes 4.22 charges. When only considering health, it pays off at 7.375 charges. When only considering mana it takes 9.86 charges. When using the Alchemist mastery the flask pays of at 3.84 charges considering both health and mana, or at 6.72 charges considering only health. Finally considering only mana the flask pays of at 8.96 charges.
Health regeneration speed is the same as a potion (10 health/s) while mana regeneration speed is a bit lower (5 MP/s vs. 6.7 MP/s)

Although many people might not compare this item to a combination of Faerie Charm and Rejuvenation Bead, it would take five minutes (180/.6) to get the same mana regen, and six minutes to get the same health regen (360/1) per set of 3 charges. Furthermore, unlike Faerie Charm and Rejuvenation Bead, which are absolutely useless while you have full or no health/mana, you can choose to use charges as long as you have them.
